title: Securing America's Ports Act
official_summary:
Securing America's Ports Act

This bill requires the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) to report to Congress a plan to perform high-throughput scanning of all commercial and passenger vehicles and freight rail traffic entering the United States at a land port of entry or rail-border crossing using large-scale non-intrusive inspection systems, such as X-ray and gamma-ray imaging systems, or similar technology. The plan shall include elements such as (1) an inventory of such systems currently in use, (2) the estimated costs of achieving a 100% scanning rate, and (3) the anticipated impact that increasing the scanning rate will have on wait times at land ports of entry and rail-border crossings. DHS shall periodically report to Congress on the progress in implementing the plan.

summary.headline: This law requires the Department of Homeland Security to create and report on a plan for scanning all vehicles and freight rail traffic entering the U.S. at land border crossings.
summary.what_it_does: The law directs DHS to report to Congress on a plan for high-throughput scanning of commercial and passenger vehicles and freight rail at land ports of entry and rail-border crossings. It uses large X-ray, gamma-ray, or similar non-intrusive inspection systems. The plan must include an inventory of current systems, estimated costs of reaching a 100% scanning rate, and expected effects on wait times. DHS must also periodically report to Congress on progress.

who_it_affects.group: U.S. Customs and Border Protection and other DHS staff
who_it_affects.how: They must build the scanning plan, inventory current equipment, estimate costs, and report progress to Congress.

who_it_affects.group: Commercial truck and freight rail operators entering the U.S. by land
who_it_affects.how: Their vehicles and rail freight would be subject to the scanning plan being developed under the law.

who_it_affects.group: Travelers driving passenger vehicles across land borders
who_it_affects.how: Their vehicles would be covered by the scanning plan, which could affect wait times at crossings.

who_it_affects.group: Communities near land ports of entry
who_it_affects.how: Wait times at local crossings are one of the required areas the plan must study, so traffic flow could be affected if scanning rates increase.
